The problem

Build a hardware pipeline for acoustic denoising that combines adaptive filtering with a learned nonlinear correction. The use cases considered include underwater acoustics and voice endpoints.

The design

An 8-tap RLS stage feeds an 8→128→384→128→1 MLP. The datapath uses signed Q1.15 fixed-point arithmetic with 40-bit accumulation. The pipeline is designed to run at 100 MHz; implementation and validation evidence need to stay tied to the numerical contract.

Architecture: reference input → 8-tap RLS → MLP correction → denoised output.

What the current simulation report says

  • RLS contribution: 5.0818 dB reported improvement.
  • MLP contribution: 3.7095 dB reported improvement.
  • Total reported improvement: 8.7913 dB.
  • Maximum hardware/software error in the report: 2.62 LSB.

These are repository-backed simulation results, not silicon measurements. They depend on the stimuli and reference implementation used in the report.

Open work

Preserve the numerical quirks in the frozen contract, reproduce the results from a clean checkout, and keep ASIC implementation claims separate from RTL simulation. The prepared patent material is a disclosure package; it is not a granted patent.
